findings.rationale: Declares the 'key insight' that frames 71-82 are airborne because the T=40 silhouette bottom 'drops to 155-177', but the Step 11 table it is reading shows frames 73-76 at 229, a bottom that never returns to the ~360-376 ground level after frame 82 (225-259 through frame 108, i.e. no landing anywhere), and a clean rise-and-return arc at frames 53-62 (364, 344, 312, 276, 241, 239, 275, 310, 355, 376) that it lumps into 'running ~230-376'; the same arc is reproduced at T=30, T=50 and in the Step 10 frame-difference output that Step 11 had dismissed as 'noisy'. This misreading fixed the search window at frames 68-91 for the rest of the run and was never revisited.

After the ASCII renders at Steps 25-27 showed the tracked component at frames 72-77 collapsing to tiny fragments at the top-left of the frame (which the agent itself called 'weird' at Step 26), it rationalizes this as a compact low-contrast 'jump apex' pose and asserts that 'various methods consistently show' the airborne phase at 71-83, citing the frame-to-frame motion gaps at 72-76 and 80-83 as evidence of flight. Loss of detection and cessation of motion are treated as proof the athlete is airborne, inverting what that evidence indicates (segmentation switching to another blob or the athlete leaving the region).

Reads the Step 28 table as 'body high/airborne' at frames 72-77 while ignoring, in the same table, that the component's x-centroid jumps from ~379 (frame 71) to ~81-282 (frames 72-77) and then to ~494-556 (frames 78-80) with top=0 at 72 and 74-77; a left-to-right runner cannot move 100-300 px backwards and touch the top edge for six frames, so the tracked blob is a different object. The contradiction recurs in the Step 31 T=5 table and is never addressed.

First detector version emitted 50/53; the agent recognized the mismatch against its target and revised (Steps 34, 37, 38 likewise emitted 22/42, 1/65, 1/5 and were revised). These are recovered iterations, not material errors on their own.

The fifth heuristic (largest-component centroid-y more than 40 px above a +/-12-frame local median, longest run wins) is adopted solely because it reproduces the presupposed 72/78 after four other heuristics did not; on the example it fires precisely because the largest component switches to a top-left blob during 72-77, so the delivered script detects a segmentation artifact rather than a flight phase, and using an unverified label as ground truth gives no basis for generalizing to other videos.

Declares the task complete stating the script 'correctly identifies' takeoff 72 and landing 78 (reaffirmed at Step 45 as 'complete and verified'), but the only confirmation performed at Steps 41-43 is that the script reproduces the agent's own hypothesis and that the TOML parses; no independent check of the jump location (x-continuity of the tracked blob, the frame-difference arc at 53-62, or inspection of actual pixels) was ever run.

notes: A correct solution had to locate the single flight phase in the example video with a method that generalizes; the agent's own outputs at Steps 10 and 11 already contained the most jump-like pattern in the whole run, a parabolic rise and return of the silhouette bottom at frames ~53-62 reproduced across frame differencing and three background thresholds. At Step 16 the agent instead read the post-71 drop of the largest-component bottom as 'airborne' even though it never returned to baseline, and at Steps 28-29 it rationalized the contradicting ASCII fragments and x-centroid jumps rather than resolving them, so every later step searched only frames 68-91. The final script was tuned until it emitted the presupposed 72/78, meaning the deliverable encodes a segmentation artifact; the process is invalid because the decisive inference contradicted evidence the agent had displayed and was never re-examined.
